back: A RAG answer about X can pass every faithfulness/citation check yet attribute entity Y's evidence to X. The checks verify citations look right, never *whose* evidence it is.
Invented sibling libraries mean no model has a prior about them, so 'which library owns this token' is deterministic, mechanical ground truth — it *replaces* the LLM judge.
Deceptive grounding 0/36 in the absent×completing cell; detectors sound (16/16). The harness works; the phenomenon is not there on this surface.
The models do not deceptively ground — they refuse or explicitly discriminate (name both X and Y). So the null is because they behave correctly, not because the detector missed anything.
M0 = fit-pilot (N=12/cell), done — the 0/36 null. M1 = the powered run, not yet run. The README is *stale*; truth is in docs/M0-BRIEF.md + data/m0_verdict.json.

front: Why may blind-cite's null be surface-specific?
back: The single-doc, name-forward setup makes Y's identity obvious, so models discriminate instead of deceiving. The paper's deception hides in multi-doc/tool-calling setups with filler — the M1 variant.

front: blind-cite: how to present it honestly
back: As in-progress: M0 validated the detectors + fabricated corpus and produced an honest early null; M1 (powered, possibly multi-doc) is unrun. Never present the pilot as finished.
